declarations.docstring: The type of modules selected by the construction associated with an R-module.
The ring type determined by an element of the opaque parameter space for R.
The opaque ring parameter selected by a simple module over a finite-dimensional algebra.
The underlying value of the parameter attached to a simple module agrees with the comparison construction.
The equivalence from modules over the selected component ring to the associated module category.
The equivalence between finite-length component-ring modules and finite-length modules satisfying the selected condition.
The forward functor of the component-module equivalence is the designated component-module functor.
Applying the component-module equivalence preserves the underlying carrier of a module.
The R-linear map from the selected component ring into the base ring.
The linear map from the selected component ring to the base ring is injective.
Mapping an element to the component ring and back to R gives left multiplication by the underlying parameter.
The linear map from the component ring to R preserves multiplication.
The image of one under the component-to-base linear map is the underlying parameter in R.
The ideal of elements annihilated by left multiplication with the underlying parameter.
The kernel ideal for left multiplication by the parameter is two-sided.
The ring homomorphism from R onto the selected component ring.
Two elements have the same image in the component ring exactly when their left multiples by the parameter agree.
The canonical homomorphism from R to the selected component ring is surjective.
The component-ring homomorphism sends the underlying parameter to one.
The functor from component-ring modules to the module category associated with the chosen simple module.
The component-module functor restricted to finite-length modules and the selected module condition.
Restriction of scalars from the selected component ring satisfies the opaque condition associated with the simple module.
The finite-length component-module functor is essentially surjective.
The component-module functor is essentially surjective.
The finite-length component-module functor is faithful.
The component-module functor is faithful.
The finite-length component-module functor is full.
The component-module functor is full.
The finite-length component-module functor is an equivalence.
The component-module functor is an equivalence.
The canonical map to the component ring carries the surjective ring-homomorphism property.
Along a surjective ring homomorphism, a module has finite length exactly when its restriction of scalars does.
A module satisfying the selected condition is torsion with respect to the left-multiplication kernel ideal.
An element belongs to the kernel ideal exactly when its left multiple by the underlying parameter is zero.
The R-linear endomorphism given by left multiplication with the underlying parameter.
The range of the component-to-base linear map consists exactly of left multiples by the underlying parameter.
The scalar-compatible linear map from the carrier of a restricted module to its original carrier.
Restriction of scalars along a surjective ring homomorphism is full.
